title: helm(private): values templating + init hooks - upgrade/rollback compatibility
author: Priya Nair
release_notes: Stabilize Helm values templating and init hook behavior across upgrades/rollbacks for private deployments. No user-facing API changes.
description: Context: Private installs using the redwood helm charts have seen intermittent failures during upgrades when init hook templating and values schema interactions change across releases. This causes init-jobs to either re-run unnecessarily on rollback or to be skipped during upgrades if templated values differ. Motivation: ensure safe, repeatable upgrades and rollbacks for on-prem/VPC customers by stabilizing values schema, improving templating determinism, and making init hooks idempotent. Changes in this PR: 1) add a stricter values.schema.json v4 that documents optional vs required fields and deprecations; 2) refactor helper templates to deterministic hashing for computed names (avoids name drift across helm render passes); 3) make init-job templates idempotent by checking existing artifacts (secrets/configmaps) and performing no-op if already satisfied; 4) introduce an init-hook manager script that records a lightweight annotation (ConfigMap) keyed by chart version+values-hash to prevent re-running the same init steps on rollback/upgrade churn; 5) add test fixtures and a small e2e job in the chart's CI to validate upgrade->rollback->upgrade flows; 6) docs updates and migration notes for older private installs. Rollout plan: merged to main, will publish chart patch v2.14.1 and coordinate with Private installer team for a staged rollout to internal canaries, then GA. See linked Linear tickets for rollout and monitoring tasks.
commits:
feat(helm): values schema v4
refactor(helm): deterministic helper tpl for computed names
fix(helm): idempotent init jobs + init-hook manager script
test(helm): add upgrade/rollback e2e fixture
docs(helm): migration notes for values schema v4
files_snippets: values.schema.json: added 'initHooks' object with 'enabled' (boolean) and 'strategy' (string enum) and marked previous 'postInit' as deprecated
_helpers.tpl: added tpl to compute stable resource name: {{- include "redwood.stableName" . -}} using sha256 of values subset
init-hook-manager.sh: record/lookup ConfigMap 'redwood-init-hooks' with key 'chart:v2.14.1|vals:<short-hash>' to avoid duplicate runs
init-job.yaml: make job check for preconditions and exit 0 if already satisfied (idempotency)
review_comments: Ethan Zhao: Can we avoid ConfigMap bloat by pruning old records? Suggest TTL logic or storing only last N entries.
Priya Nair: Added pruning logic to init-hook-manager.sh (keeps last 10 entries) and documented it in the migration notes.
Rafaela Martins: Please add a unit test for the deterministic name helper to prevent regressions.
Priya Nair: Added a small template unit test in chart test harness under tests/helpers/name.stest.
Jonah Kim: CI failed on first run due to missing bash dependency in the helm test image; switched to alpine image with bash and re-ran; all green.
Rafaela Martins: Approving after verifying e2e upgrade->rollback->upgrade flow on internal canary cluster.
Ethan Zhao: One nit: update Chart.yaml annotations to include migration note for v2.14.1. Done.
merge_outcome: Merged to main after approvals and green CI. Will publish chart package and follow rollout checklist.
notes_for_ops: Operators should follow docs/helm/private-upgrade-rollback.md. On large installs, enable chart option 'initHooks.prune.expected=true' to avoid ConfigMap growth. Monitor init-hook-run_count metric and the 'redwood_init_hook_errors' alert. Rolling back to a pre-v2.14.1 chart will not re-run init steps if values-hash matches; to force re-run set 'initHooks.forceReapply=true'.
changelog_entry: chart(redwood-private): stabilize values schema v4 and make init hooks idempotent; add upgrade/rollback e2e tests; migration notes for private installs.
notes: This PR was coordinated with the Private Installer team, SRE, and security to ensure no secrets are persisted by the init-hook manager. The values.schema change is additive; existing installs will be validated and will require manual opt-in for deprecated fields.
